test_policy.notes: "Pratt is test optional": SAT or ACT scores are not required, and applicants who send them do so directly from the College Board or ACT. Merit scholarships for high school applicants are based on GPA and portfolio only. CDS C8 agrees (scores 'not required for admission, but considered if submitted'; test scores 'not considered' in the C7 factor grid).

requirements.supplemental_essays: Required Pratt essay of 250-500 words (the Common App essay is optional): write about a piece of work (visual art, music, writing, architecture or design) that influenced you, or a piece of your own work and its impact on you. AI text-generation tools are not permitted in any written application material.
requirements.portfolio: Required for the art, design, architecture, film and writing programs: a general visual portfolio of 10-20 recent works (made within the last 18 months) including 3-5 drawings from direct observation; Film adds a short video or visual portfolio plus a writing component; Writing needs up to 10 pages of creative writing; the BA in Critical & Visual Studies and BA in History of Art & Design need 5-10 pages of writing. Construction Management needs no portfolio. Images fully generated by AI are prohibited.
requirements.notes: Common App. Application fee $50 for U.S. citizens and permanent residents and $90 for international applicants (the $50 is shown as the fee). The CDS (C13) says the fee can be waived for applicants with financial need; the requirements page does not describe a waiver, so that field is left blank. Letters of recommendation are optional (up to three, not from family or friends; the CDS rates recommendations 'important'). Official transcripts must come directly from the school through an approved service; documents not in English need a NACES-certified translation; official external exam results (IB, A-levels, GCSE, French Bac...) are required if the school mandated them for graduation. The pages mention no interview and no counselor letter or mid-year report, so those fields are left blank. Applicants to Architecture, Writing, Critical & Visual Studies, History of Art & Design (BA) and Construction Management must choose the major when applying; applicants to the schools of Art and Design can apply undecided and choose in the spring of the first year (2D Animation and Game Arts may not be available to undecided students). Pratt says citizenship or visa status does not factor into the admissions review.

deadlines.label: Early Action
deadlines.notes: Non-binding (CDS C22: not restrictive). Complete the application with all required materials; decision "by mid-December" (no exact date published). The page prints month and day only; the requirements page says "Applications for Fall 2027 are now open", so fall 2027 entry is read. No separate international deadline is published.

deadlines.label: Priority decision date
deadlines.notes: Priority date to complete the application; decision within 3 weeks of a complete application. Month and day only on the page; fall 2027 entry assumed.

deadlines.label: Regular Decision: rolling after January 15
deadlines.notes: "After January 15, applications continue to be reviewed on a rolling basis" for admission and scholarship decisions, decision within 3 weeks of a complete application; spaces in programs may become limited in February and March. No final closing date is printed. Spring entry (Oct. 1, Sept. 1 recommended for international students) is open only to Construction Management, Writing, Critical & Visual Studies, History of Art and Design (BA) and AOS programs.

english_policy.waiver_notes: Required of international applicants and anyone whose primary or native language is not English. Waiver (reviewed at the Office of Admissions' discretion) if the applicant studied the last three years of high school in the U.S., in a country where English is the official national language and primary language of instruction, or at an English-speaking school in a non-English-speaking country that is U.S.-accredited or an English-speaking IB World school, all in good academic standing; ESL programs or certificates do not count. Scores must be sent by the testing agency before the deadline and taken within two years of the start term (for fall 2027, on or after August 2025). TOEFL MyBest scores are not accepted.

english.notes: Page: "TOEFL IBT and TOEFL Home Edition: minimum score of 92 in the 0-120 scale, or 5 in the new 1-6 scale". MyBest scores not accepted. Pratt submission code 2669. No subscore minimums listed.
New 1-6 scale minimum as printed (5). Submission code 2669.
IELTS Academic, minimum overall 7.0 as printed. No subscore minimums listed.
Duolingo English Test, minimum score 125 as printed.
PTE Academic, minimum score 62 as printed.
Cambridge English Proficiency (C1 or C2 levels), minimum score 183 as printed.

aid.notes: Pratt says "International students do not qualify for need-based aid" and are not eligible for federal aid (do not file the FAFSA). "All international applicants who are admitted will be automatically evaluated for merit-based scholarship", with no separate application; any award is in the acceptance letter, and it rests on a holistic review of the application (for high school applicants GPA and portfolio, since Pratt is test-optional). Presidential merit scholarships are renewable with a 2.5 GPA. The Common Data Set (H6) ticks both need-based and non-need-based institutional aid for nonresidents and reports 620 recipients averaging $19,224, which conflicts with the scholarship page; the college's own page wording is used for the policy. CDS H7 checks only the International Student's Certification of Finances (not the CSS Profile or Pratt's own aid form) as the form nonresident first-year aid applicants must submit. The freshman net price calculator cannot be used by international students. Pratt's 2026-27 cost of attendance for a resident is $90,967 (cost-of-attendance PDF).

majors.notes: Must be chosen when applying (different first-year curriculum from other majors); general visual portfolio. Architecture drew 1,073 first-time undergraduate applicants in fall 2025 (18% of applicants, Quick Facts, which excludes Munson).

majors.program: Art and Design BFA programs (School of Art, School of Design)
majors.notes: Applicants choose a BFA major (the requirements page lists, among others, Art & Design Education, 2D and 3D Animation, Digital Arts & Technology, Drawing, Fashion Design, Game Arts, Graphic Design, History Art & Design (BFA), Illustration, Industrial Design, Interior Design, Jewelry, Painting, Sculpture and Integrated Practices, Photography, Printmaking and Film) when applying; general visual portfolio. 2D Animation and Game Arts should be chosen at application because they may not be available to undecided students.

majors.program: Undecided (School of Art and School of Design)
majors.notes: Applicants unsure of a major can apply undecided, complete the Foundation year and choose a major in the spring of the first year.

majors.program: Writing (BFA), Critical & Visual Studies (BA), History of Art & Design (BA)
majors.notes: Major chosen at application; Writing submits up to 10 pages of creative writing, the BA programs 5-10 pages of writing.
Major chosen at application; no portfolio, and merit scholarships are based on GPA only. Can start in the spring semester.

tier_notes.general: Pratt is a leading art, design and architecture college, but it offers only a few non-studio majors; with an 86% admit rate (CDS C1, fall 2025) and SAT middle 50% 1140-1380 for the submitters, the overall letter sits with RIT, Drexel and Stevens (C+); editorial judgment against the existing peers.
tier_notes.arts_design: A: among the strongest art, design and architecture schools in the country (Architecture, Communications Design and Fashion Design draw the most applicants), but not at RISD's level; editorial judgment, no ranking source cited.
tier_notes.humanities: D: Writing (BFA), Critical & Visual Studies (BA) and History of Art & Design (BA) are small programs; editorial judgment.
tier_notes.computer_science: No computer science degree (digital arts and game arts are BFA studio majors).
tier_notes.engineering: No engineering program (Architecture is a design degree).
tier_notes.business: No business program; Construction Management (BS) is the closest.
tier_notes.pre_med: No pre-med track or science major.
